narrativeReportMd:
# Address R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local hard instance-breaking change was found for `Address`: the same local elements exist in R4 and R6 with unchanged cardinalities, datatypes, modifier flags, summary flags, and required code sets. The meaningful local changes are low-impact semantic/conformance text updates around coded string representation, display newline formatting, and ISO 3166 country-code guidance.

## Scope
The analysis covered the core `Address` datatype StructureDefinitions and the required `address-use` and `address-type` bindings. Inherited datatype infrastructure changes, including the R6 `DataType` base class and inherited `extension` behavior, are out of scope and should be handled by the base-artifact reports.

## Main migration themes
Existing R4 `Address` JSON/XML element shapes should continue to validate structurally in R6. Implementers should review display and normalization code rather than database schemas: R6 now explicitly describes `Address.text` as newline-delimited by line, clarifies that two- or three-letter ISO 3166 country codes may be used, and mentions ISO21090-codedString for coded representations of Address strings.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no Critical or High findings. The highest-impact item is the new ISO21090-codedString statement because it can influence extension handling and round-trip behavior even though no new local element or invariant was added.

## Findings requiring human review
The ISO21090-codedString guidance deserves review because the R6 core package text mentions it but no `StructureDefinition-iso21090-codedString.json` was found in the supplied R6 package.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The observed changes are mostly clarifications and were made in a backward-compatible structural way. Where risk exists, it comes from narrative conformance expectations or optional extension use rather than from validators rejecting existing R4 instances.

## Follow-up analysis
Base datatype reports should cover the R6 `DataType` hierarchy and inherited extension/constraint changes. Official narrative diff pages and ballot change notes would improve confidence in the intended normative force of the semantic text changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Address` has no local hard R4→R6 instance break. Migration attention should focus on low-impact semantic guidance for ISO21090-codedString, newline-delimited `Address.text`, and ISO 3166 country-code interpretation; the main uncertainty is the absence of official diff/narrative change notes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Element shape is stable, so schema and generated-class migrations should be light for `Address` itself. Validators and code generators should still refresh package versions so required binding URLs point at R6, but enum members for `Address.use` and `Address.type` were unchanged. Rendering, normalization, and cross-version transformation code should avoid assuming `Address.text` is a single-line label and should decide how to treat R6 coded string extensions if encountered.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable structural conclusions because both primary StructureDefinitions were present and the local element lists matched exactly. Confidence is medium for the semantic intent of narrative text changes because official diffs, ballot rationale, and full rendered specification pages were not supplied. Terminology confidence is high enough for this report because both local CodeSystems are complete and contain the same codes, though no external terminology expansion was run.

findings.title: Address root definition now mentions ISO21090-codedString for coded string content

oldState.summary: R4 described Address as a postal-convention datatype without ISO21090-codedString guidance.

semanticText.definition: An address expressed using postal conventions ... There are a variety of postal address formats defined around the world.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 root definition describes postal address use and format variety, but does not tell implementers to use ISO21090-codedString for coded string content.

newState.summary: R6 adds root-level guidance that ISO21090-codedString may provide coded representations of strings in Address.

semanticText.definition: An address expressed using postal conventions ... The ISO21090-codedString may be used to provide a coded representation of the contents of strings in an Address.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 root definition keeps the R4 postal-address description and adds a new statement allowing ISO21090-codedString to represent coded content of strings in an Address.

facts.newValue: Adds: The ISO21090-codedString may be used to provide a coded representation of the contents of strings in an Address.
Still no dedicated coded string element; guidance is narrative/extension-oriented.

facts.oldValue: R4 package contains several iso21090 extension StructureDefinitions but not iso21090-codedString.
facts.newValue: No StructureDefinition named iso21090-codedString was found in the supplied R6 core package.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The finding compares the same root element id `Address` in the R4 and R6 differentials. The only local computable change at this location is the added definition sentence.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a direct validation break: no element, cardinality, type, invariant, or required binding changed. The risk is runtime and round-trip oriented. R6 senders may place coded representations in primitive extensions on `Address` strings, and R4 receivers or converters that whitelist only known R4 core extensions may drop or reject those extensions even though base FHIR extension syntax can carry them.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Loss of coded address-string annotations could affect administrative normalization or jurisdictional address processing, but the core postal address text remains available.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow structured/coded annotations for otherwise free-text Address string components without adding new local Address elements.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed because the change is optional narrative guidance and preserves the R4 Address element model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--allowing coded annotations on otherwise free-text address strings--is reasonable, and R6 accomplishes it without adding required elements, removing existing fields, or narrowing any R4-valid `Address` instance. The compatibility concern is mainly R6-to-R4 preservation of optional primitive extensions and uncertainty about the referenced extension artifact, not old-valid/new-invalid base validation breakage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the actual R6 base design keeps the R4 wire shape, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is **Not applicable** rather than `Partial`. A canonical extension definition and explicit cross-version guidance would be helpful, but those would mitigate ambiguity for implementers and converters; they are not a less-breaking base model needed to preserve R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Publishing a clearer extension artifact or cross-version note would reduce ambiguity, but that is interoperability guidance rather than a backward-compatible base-design alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 root definition lacks ISO21090-codedString guidance.
evidence.quote: There are a variety of postal address formats defined around the world.

evidence.detail: R6 root definition adds ISO21090-codedString guidance.
evidence.quote: The ISO21090-codedString may be used to provide a coded representation of the contents of strings in an Address.

evidence.sourceRef: R6 package index and file search
evidence.detail: No matching R6 core StructureDefinition file was found in the supplied package.

examples.examplesMd: An R6 sender might attach a coded-string extension to primitive string values such as `line`, `city`, or `country`. The base string value remains representable in R4, but strict R4 extension allow-lists may need explicit policy for preserving or rejecting the coded annotation.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a root-level statement that ISO21090-codedString may be used for coded representations of strings inside `Address`. This does not add a new field and should not invalidate existing R4 addresses. It can still surprise implementers because it changes the expected extension vocabulary around primitive address strings, while the supplied R6 core package did not include a matching `iso21090-codedString` StructureDefinition.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A plain R4 `Address` instance remains structurally valid against the local R6 `Address` shape. The compatibility issue appears when an R6 instance uses coded primitive-string extensions: R4 can syntactically carry extensions, but R4 validators or generated models with strict known-extension handling may reject or drop the coded annotation. This is therefore not old-valid/new-invalid; it is an R6-to-R4 preservation and runtime policy risk.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Migration tools should preserve unknown primitive extensions on `Address` string elements unless local policy requires rejection. If coded address annotations matter, add explicit tests for `_line`, `_city`, `_state`, `_postalCode`, and `_country` extension round-tripping. Human review should confirm the intended canonical extension URL before mapping coded content into local models.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is structurally backward-compatible because it uses FHIR's extension mechanism rather than adding mandatory elements. The avoidable part is ambiguity: a published extension artifact and cross-version note would let R4/R6 converters recognize the feature without inferring behavior from a root definition sentence.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review the official R6 narrative or ballot materials for the canonical status of ISO21090-codedString; the local R6 core package search did not find a corresponding StructureDefinition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional root-level guidance that ISO21090-codedString may be used for coded representations of string contents in Address. The Address element model itself is unchanged: no path, cardinality, type, invariant, modifier flag, or binding change makes an R4 Address invalid or changes generated Address properties. The missing local StructureDefinition for iso21090-codedString makes the guidance less clear, but that is a documentation/tooling ambiguity rather than a base R4-to-R6 compatibility break.
keyEvidence: R4 Address root definition ends with general postal-format guidance and has no ISO21090-codedString sentence.
R6 Address root definition adds: The ISO21090-codedString may be used to provide a coded representation of the contents of strings in an Address.
R4 and R6 Address snapshots keep the same local child elements and no computable restriction was added at Address.
R6 package index/file search found no StructureDefinition file named for iso21090-codedString in the supplied core package.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 Address is normative, so prose changes deserve scrutiny. Here the stability concern is softened by the optional may-language and the absence of a computable conformance change.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: optional guidance was added, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid instance break or generated API/codegen change for Address.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed to preserve R4 instances. A clearer canonical extension reference or non-normative implementation note could reduce ambiguity, but it would not materially improve wire compatibility because the base model did not become stricter.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing low-impact/no-hard-break assessment and no less-breaking-alternative finding; I would downplay the reported R6-to-R4 risk because the local evidence shows optional prose rather than a new computable feature.

findings.title: Address.text definition now specifies newline-delimited display lines

oldState.summary: R4 allowed a text representation of the entire address without specifying a line delimiter.

semanticText.definition: Specifies the entire address as it should be displayed e.g. on a postal label. This may be provided instead of or as well as the specific parts.
semanticText.comment: Can provide both a text representation and parts. Applications updating an address SHALL ensure that when both text and parts are present, no content is included in the text that isn't found in a part.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 treats `Address.text` as the displayable full address but does not define how multiple display lines are delimited within the string.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same `string` field but says display lines use newline delimiters such as `\n`.

semanticText.definition: Specifies the entire address as it should be displayed e.g. on a postal label, using a newline delimiter for each line (e.g., \n). This may be provided instead of or as well as the specific parts.
semanticText.comment: Can provide both a text representation and parts. Applications updating an address SHALL ensure that when both text and parts are present, no content is included in the text that isn't found in a part.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps `Address.text` optional and typed as `string`, but adds normative-looking display guidance that each postal-label line is separated with a newline delimiter.

facts.newValue: Adds newline delimiter guidance for each display line.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id `Address.text` exists in both differentials with unchanged cardinality and type; only the definition text changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: FHIR validators normally enforce the primitive string type and cardinality, not the exact postal-label line delimiter. Existing R4 single-line or differently delimited text remains syntactically valid, but R6 renderers, normalizers, or conformance tests may start interpreting `\n` as the preferred line boundary.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect address display can affect mailing labels and administrative workflows, but the change does not alter address-part data.

justification.inferredGoal: Standardize how the full text address is rendered as multiple postal-label lines.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed because the element remains the same optional string and R4 values remain structurally valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--standardizing multi-line postal-label display in `Address.text`--is reasonable, and the R6 change does not alter cardinality, type, or serialization. Existing R4 text strings remain representable; the risk is behavioral interpretation by renderers or profile-specific tests, so the level of base breakage is low.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The previous report's `Partial` alternative of using examples or non-normative guidance is better understood as a softer specification choice, not a necessary backward-compatible base-design alternative. Since R6 did not introduce a structural or validator-enforced break, the alternative judgment is **Not applicable**. Implementers may still need migration guidance for rendering behavior.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Softer examples could reduce conformance surprise, but they would also weaken the standardization goal and are not needed to preserve R4 instances.

evidence.detail: R4 describes the full display text without line-delimiter guidance.
evidence.quote: Specifies the entire address as it should be displayed e.g. on a postal label.
using a newline delimiter for each line (e.g., \n)

examples.examplesMd: The example shows the R6-preferred display-line convention. It is illustrative and not a complete resource or standalone datatype validation fixture.

findings.narrativeMd: `Address.text` did not change shape, but R6 now states that line breaks in the full postal-label representation use newline delimiters. Systems that treated `text` as an opaque single-line string, HTML fragment, comma-delimited label, or locale-specific display blob may still validate but behave differently when interoperating with R6 systems expecting newline-separated lines.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is still-valid-but-behaviorally-different rather than a hard validation break. R4-valid strings are not rejected by the R6 StructureDefinition solely because they omit `\n`, but display code, snapshot tests, or profile-specific assertions could become stricter. R6 newline-delimited text is directly representable in R4 as a string.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not split or rewrite historical `Address.text` blindly. For new R6 output, emit newline-delimited postal-label lines where multiple display lines are intended. Add rendering tests that cover single-line text, newline-delimited multi-line text, and consistency between `text` and structured parts.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is mostly backward-compatible because it standardizes string content rather than the element model. A softer alternative would have been an example or implementation note; that would reduce conformance surprise but leave ambiguity for postal-label rendering.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 clarifies how multiple display lines should be represented inside the existing Address.text string. The field remains optional, single-valued, typed as string, and summary-only as before. Existing R4 payloads do not become structurally invalid; at most, renderers or local conformance checks may prefer newline-separated labels for better postal display.
keyEvidence: R4 Address.text definition describes the entire display address without delimiter guidance.
R6 Address.text definition adds newline delimiter guidance for each line, e.g. \n.
R4 and R6 Address.text both remain 0..1 string with the same summary status and no binding or invariant.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 Address is normative, which raises the threshold for disruptive changes. This change is only display-format guidance on an unchanged string, so normative status does not make it a material compatibility issue.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: possible local rendering or warning-as-error policy effects, but no base validator, wire-format, or generated-model break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A softer example or note could have reduced perceived conformance pressure, but there is no meaningful less-breaking base design to preserve because old string values remain representable. Making a formal delimiter invariant would be more breaking, not less.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low-impact and no-hard-break assessment; the practical concern is limited to local rendering/normalization choices rather than base compatibility.

findings.title: Address.country comment now explicitly permits ISO 3166 two- or three-letter codes

oldState.summary: R4 type was string; short text mentioned 2- or 3-letter ISO 3166 codes, while the comment specifically mentioned 3-letter codes.

semanticText.short: Country (e.g. can be ISO 3166 2 or 3 letter code)
semanticText.definition: Country - a nation as commonly understood or generally accepted.
semanticText.comment: ISO 3166 3 letter codes can be used in place of a human readable country name.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had mixed guidance: the short description allowed two- or three-letter ISO 3166 codes, but the comment singled out three-letter codes as the alternative to a human-readable country name.

newState.summary: R6 keeps string shape and clarifies in the comment that ISO 3166 two- or three-letter codes MAY be used.

semanticText.short: Country (e.g. may be ISO 3166 2 or 3 letter code)
semanticText.definition: Country - a nation as commonly understood or generally accepted.
semanticText.comment: ISO 3166 2- or 3- letter codes MAY be used in place of a human readable country name.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 aligns the short text and comment by explicitly permitting either two- or three-letter ISO 3166 codes.

facts.oldValue: ISO 3166 3 letter codes can be used in place of a human readable country name.
facts.newValue: ISO 3166 2- or 3- letter codes MAY be used in place of a human readable country name.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same `Address.country` element exists in both versions with unchanged cardinality, string type, and no terminology binding.

impact.impactRationaleMd: There is no computable validation break because `country` remains an unconstrained `string`. The practical risk is with business rules or UI validation that interpreted the R4 comment as preferring or requiring three-letter codes and may reject R6 data using two-letter codes such as `US` or `DE`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Country-code normalization can affect administrative routing and matching, but the element remains a string and can also carry human-readable names.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify ambiguous R4 country-code guidance and align the comment with the existing short description.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No backward-compatible alternative is needed because the change clarifies and widens existing string guidance rather than narrowing the base model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--aligning the country comment with R4's existing short description that already mentioned two- or three-letter ISO 3166 codes--is reasonable. R6 keeps `Address.country` as an unconstrained optional string, so R4-valid country names and codes remain base-valid while two-letter code guidance becomes clearer.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This is a widening/clarification that preserves R4 instances, so `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is **Not applicable** under the calibration rules. The notable alternative would have been a coded type or required binding, but that would be stricter and less compatible, not a less-breaking way to meet the stated goal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: A formal ISO 3166 binding would improve consistency but would be more breaking; the chosen text clarification avoids that tradeoff.

evidence.detail: R4 comment names only three-letter ISO 3166 codes.
evidence.quote: ISO 3166 3 letter codes can be used in place of a human readable country name.

evidence.detail: R6 comment explicitly permits two- or three-letter ISO 3166 codes and uses RFC-style MAY language.
evidence.quote: ISO 3166 2- or 3- letter codes MAY be used in place of a human readable country name.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is representable in R4 as a string and was arguably already allowed by the R4 short description. It may still fail local R4-era business rules that used the R4 comment to require ISO 3166 alpha-3 values.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 explicitly permits ISO 3166 two- or three-letter country codes in `Address.country`. Because the element remains a plain string and R4's short text already mentioned two-letter codes, this is best understood as a clarification/widening of guidance, not a base validation change. The migration risk is in local normalization rules, enum-like wrappers, or UI validators that were stricter than the base R4 StructureDefinition.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Base FHIR validation does not reject R4 or R6 country strings on this basis. R6 content using two-letter codes is structurally representable in R4, but may not be semantically accepted by systems that only allowed human-readable names or ISO alpha-3 codes. This is a local business-rule compatibility risk rather than a StructureDefinition hard break.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review country normalization code and tests. If a system stores canonical country codes, accept both ISO 3166 alpha-2 and alpha-3 on input and normalize according to local policy. Do not introduce a required code binding unless a profile explicitly narrows `Address.country`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The clarification is backward-compatible at the core model level. A stricter coded datatype or required binding would have made country handling more uniform but would have broken the intentionally flexible string representation used for postal addresses worldwide.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 aligns the country-code prose by explicitly allowing ISO 3166 two- or three-letter codes using MAY language. Address.country remains an unconstrained optional string with no terminology binding, so R4 country values remain valid and R6 two-letter values are still just string content for cross-version exchange.
keyEvidence: R4 Address.country is 0..1 string with no binding; its short text already mentions ISO 3166 two- or three-letter codes.
R4 Address.country comment specifically mentions three-letter ISO 3166 codes.
R6 Address.country keeps 0..1 string with no binding and changes the comment to permit ISO 3166 2- or 3-letter codes MAY be used.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 Address is normative, so I checked for a computable narrowing. None exists; the change is permissive clarification on an unchanged string.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: local country-code business rules may need review, but base FHIR validation and serialization are unchanged.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking alternative is needed. Keeping the string while clarifying permitted code forms is already compatibility-preserving; a required ISO 3166 binding would be stricter and more breaking.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low-impact/no-hard-break assessment and the absence of a less-breaking base-design alternative.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, status, and abstract flag remain aligned. The baseDefinition shift to `DataType` is explicitly out of scope as a base-artifact issue.

The local differential element ids are the same: `Address`, `use`, `type`, `text`, `line`, `city`, `district`, `state`, `postalCode`, `country`, and `period`. Snapshot `Address.id` and `Address.extension` are inherited and unchanged in presence.
All local cardinalities are unchanged, including `Address.use/type/text/city/district/state/postalCode/country/period` as `0..1` and `Address.line` as `0..*`.
Local type codes are unchanged: `use` and `type` are `code`, text and address parts are `string`, and `period` is `Period`. There are no choice-type additions or removals.

`Address.use` and `Address.type` remain required bindings. The bound ValueSet versions changed from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4`, but local complete CodeSystems contain the same codes and definitions.
No local Address-specific invariant was added or removed. Inherited constraint presentation differences, including XPath metadata and inherited extension constraints, are base-artifact scope.
`Address.use` remains `isModifier=true` with the same modifier reason. Other local elements are not modifiers.
Summary flags are unchanged for all local elements checked.
No fixed, pattern, or default value constraints were found on local Address elements in either version.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex-style value limit changes were found.
No local Address element gained or lost slicing. Inherited extension slicing is base-artifact scope.
No local element names, primitive/complex representations, or choice suffixes changed, so generated property names and JSON/XML shapes for Address itself remain stable.
R6 did not add local Address elements or required codes that R4 cannot carry. The only representability caveat is optional coded-string extension use implied by new R6 narrative text.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Required binding ValueSet URLs now reference the R6 ballot package version
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding strength remains `required` and local complete CodeSystems for `address-use` and `address-type` have the same code members and definitions in R4 and R6. Existing base-valid R4 codes remain valid under the R6 bindings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators and validators should refresh the bound ValueSet version strings from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4`, but enum members do not need data migration based on the supplied package content.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Address.type comment adds guidance about collections and implicit purpose
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Address.type` remains optional `0..1`, typed as `code`, and bound to the same `postal | physical | both` code set. The new comment explains when the element is useful or typically omitted; it does not add a validator-enforced rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Profile authors and UI designers should review whether `Address.type` is redundant when an element or extension already implies postal/physical purpose. Existing instances do not need structural migration.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Address` now derives from `DataType` instead of directly from `Element`. That class-hierarchy/codegen impact is intentionally excluded here and should be assessed in the `DataType` or base datatype report.
Snapshot differences on inherited `id`/`extension` constraints and XPath metadata are not local Address findings but may matter to validators and generated base classes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4→R6 diff, ballot rationale, or change-request/Jira trail was supplied. This limits assessment of why the semantic text changed and whether it was intended to be normative or explanatory.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Compare against official HL7 rendered diff pages or approved ballot change notes for the Address datatype.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis used packaged StructureDefinition text rather than rendered specification narrative pages. Rendered pages may include additional notes, examples, warnings, or extension references that clarify the semantic changes.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Inspect the R4 and R6 rendered Address datatype pages and any linked extension documentation.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No terminology-server expansion was run. Required binding conclusions rely on local ValueSet.compose and complete local CodeSystem content, which was sufficient for the simple Address use/type code systems but not equivalent to a server expansion audit.
